statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON (green). Tail 19 (low), Stress 40 (moderate), Confidence 88 (high). The Nasdaq-100 closed at a record with observed trend-up structure, but the cash session has ended and CME index futures are in their 20:00-21:00Z maintenance break.
recommendation: Tail remains below the block threshold for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD. The narrow evidence-based danger window is the Sep 23 US cash open combined with the 13:45Z S&P Global flash PMIs, where the forecast maps to WATCH. Existing-position management and emergency protection remain unaffected by this assessment.
headline: Nasdaq-100 settles at a record 30,732.40 (+0.82%) with VIX at 14.25; overnight path risk low, Sep 23 open plus flash PMIs flagged
body: The Nasdaq-100 closed the Sep 22 US cash session at 30,732.40, up 0.82%, opening at the 30,496.43 session low and settling 38 points (0.12%) below the 30,770.63 high - a second consecutive record Nasdaq close. Leadership was narrow: the S&P 500 finished flat and the Dow fell 0.36%. Directional efficiency into the close was genuine, but the session path included a mid-morning acceleration on Iran/Hormuz headlines followed by a partial reversal on subsequent UN remarks, so meaningful retracement was available rather than absent. Cross-assets are supportive rather than stressed: VIX 14.25 (-4.2%), WTI near $89-90 after a fifth lower session, Brent below $100. The rate backdrop is the standing constraint - the 10-year Treasury at 4.96% and the 2-year at 4.76% (H.15, Sep 21), with Richmond Fed President Barkin describing supply shocks as no longer short-lived and leaving further hikes open after last week's increase. Delayed latest-session context showed all seven tracked semiconductors higher and megacaps split four-four, consistent with narrow, chip-led strength. With the cash session closed and futures in their maintenance break, the probability of a path that denies mean reversion is low for the immediate hours; the conditional concentration point is the Sep 23 cash open at 13:30Z immediately followed by S&P Global flash PMIs at 13:45Z.

lookbackSummary: The trailing 24 published hours are complete. Overnight Sep 21-22 held Tail 11-14 in normal conditions. Tail stepped to 21 at 14:00Z on the US open, eased to 14-17 through the mixed midday, then returned to 20-21 (WATCH) from 18:00Z as the index pressed toward its record settlement. No hour reached the block threshold.
outlookSummary: Overnight Tail is expected to hold in the 12-15 band through Asia and early Europe, with mode normal and no scheduled US catalysts. Scores step up through the European session and concentrate at the Sep 23 US cash open (13:30Z) and S&P Global flash PMIs (13:45Z), where the forecast reaches Tail 21 (WATCH) in event/whipsaw mode, then decays through the afternoon as post-event price discovery is assumed to normalise. Confidence declines with distance from the evidence cutoff.
